syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Features and Kinds of Companies

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the special features of a company such as separate legal entity, limited liability and perpetual succession.
Distinguish companies by the liability of members and by the number of members, including the One Person Company.

topics.title: Share Capital and its Categories

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish authorised, issued, subscribed, called-up, paid-up, uncalled and reserve capital.
Show share capital correctly in the Notes to Accounts of a company's balance sheet.

topics.title: Nature and Classes of Shares

concepts.learning_objective: State the preferential rights that define a preference share under Section 43 of the Companies Act, 2013.
Explain the rights of equity shareholders in dividend and in repayment of capital.

topics.title: Issue of Shares

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the steps of a share issue: prospectus, receipt of applications and allotment.
Apply the minimum subscription rule to decide whether a company may allot shares.
Explain how Applications Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA) work for application money.

topics.title: Journal Entries for Application, Allotment and Calls

concepts.learning_objective: Record journal entries for application, allotment and calls on shares issued at par.
Apply Table F rules on the amount, interval and notice of calls.
Account for calls in arrears and calls in advance, including interest on them.

topics.title: Over Subscription, Premium and Shares for Consideration other than Cash

concepts.learning_objective: Account for over subscription by rejection, pro-rata allotment or both, and for under subscription.
Record shares issued at a premium and state the uses of Securities Premium and the limits on issue at a discount.
Calculate and record shares issued to vendors for consideration other than cash.

topics.title: Forfeiture and Reissue of Shares

concepts.learning_objective: Record the forfeiture of shares issued at par or at a premium.
Record the reissue of forfeited shares and work out the amount transferred to capital reserve.

topics.title: Meaning of debentures and distinction from shares

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a debenture as a written acknowledgement of debt and part of borrowed capital.
Distinguish between shares and debentures on ownership, return, repayment, voting rights, security and convertibility.

topics.title: Types of debentures

concepts.learning_objective: Classify debentures as secured or unsecured and as redeemable or irredeemable.
Classify debentures by convertibility, coupon rate and registration.

topics.title: Issue of debentures for cash and over subscription

concepts.learning_objective: Record the issue of debentures for cash at par, at a discount and at a premium.
Account for excess application money adjusted towards allotment and refunds on rejected applications.

topics.title: Issue of debentures for consideration other than cash

concepts.learning_objective: Record debentures issued to vendors at par, premium or discount and compute the number of debentures issued.
Determine goodwill or capital reserve when purchase consideration differs from net assets taken over.

topics.title: Issue of debentures as collateral security

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of collateral security and the lender's rights over debentures so issued.
Show debentures issued as collateral security under the note method and the Debenture Suspense method.

topics.title: Terms of issue and redemption of debentures

concepts.learning_objective: Compute the loss on issue of debentures under different combinations of issue and redemption terms.
Explain the treatment of premium on redemption of debentures as a liability.

topics.title: Interest on debentures

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate interest on debentures on their nominal value and record its transfer to the Statement of Profit and Loss.
Record tax deducted at source on debenture interest and its payment to the government.

topics.title: Writing off discount or loss on issue of debentures

concepts.learning_objective: Write off discount or loss on issue of debentures first from Securities Premium Reserve and then from the Statement of Profit and Loss.

topics.title: Meaning and nature of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: State what financial statements are and which statements they include.
Explain how recorded facts, conventions, postulates and personal judgements shape financial statements.

topics.title: Objectives of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the primary objective of financial statements is to assist users in decision-making.
Identify the specific objectives of financial statements and match them to users' needs.

topics.title: Form of balance sheet and shareholders' funds under Schedule III

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the heads, sub-heads and presentation features of the balance sheet under Schedule III.
Show share capital, calls-in-arrears and forfeited shares in the balance sheet and notes to accounts.
Compute and present reserves and surplus, including a debit balance of the statement of profit and loss.

topics.title: Current and non-current classification of balance sheet items

concepts.learning_objective: State the criteria for classifying an item as current or non-current.
Classify borrowings, trade payables, provisions and deferred tax under the correct heads.
Classify fixed assets, investments, inventories and trade receivables under the correct heads.

topics.title: Form and content of the statement of profit and loss

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish revenue from operations from other income.
Place expenses under the correct heads of the statement of profit and loss.
Compute profit before tax in the Schedule III format.

topics.title: Uses and importance of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how different users rely on financial statements for their decisions.

topics.title: Limitations of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain limitations arising from historical cost and the realisable value of assets.
Explain limitations of bias, aggregation, missing and qualitative information, and interim reporting.

topics.title: Meaning of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that financial analysis combines analysis (simplifying and classifying data) with interpretation (explaining its meaning and significance).
Distinguish comparison with other firms (cross-sectional analysis) from comparison with the firm's own past performance (time series analysis).

topics.title: Significance of financial analysis to its users

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the finance manager and top management use financial analysis for decisions and control.
Identify what trade payables, lenders, investors, labour unions and others look for when they analyse financial statements.

topics.title: Objectives of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: State the objectives of financial analysis such as judging profitability, relative importance of components, reasons for change and debt-repaying ability.
Explain how economists and government use the analysis of corporate financial statements.

topics.title: Tools of analysis of financial statements

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish comparative statements (horizontal analysis) from common size statements (vertical analysis).
Calculate and interpret trend percentages with reference to a base year.
Describe the purpose of ratio analysis and cash flow analysis as tools of financial analysis.

topics.title: Comparative statements

concepts.learning_objective: Prepare and interpret comparative statements of profit and loss and comparative balance sheets.
Calculate absolute and percentage changes between two years in a comparative statement.

topics.title: Common size statements

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the common base used in common size statements of profit and loss and balance sheets.
Calculate common size percentages and use them for intra-firm and inter-firm comparison.

topics.title: Limitations of financial analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that financial analysis ignores price level changes and non-monetary aspects of a business.
Explain how changes in accounting policies and window dressing can make financial analysis misleading.

topics.title: Meaning, objectives and advantages of ratio analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what an accounting ratio is and why it must relate meaningfully connected figures.
State the objectives for which ratio analysis is carried out.
Identify the advantages of ratio analysis and its indicative, whistle-blowing role.

topics.title: Limitations of ratio analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how limitations of financial statements, such as ignored price-level changes and varied practices, limit ratio analysis.
Identify the limitations of ratios themselves, such as lack of standard definitions and standard levels.

topics.title: Types of ratios

concepts.learning_objective: Classify ratios as statement of profit and loss, balance sheet or composite ratios.
Classify ratios as liquidity, solvency, activity or profitability ratios by their purpose.

topics.title: Liquidity ratios

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate and interpret the current ratio.
Calculate and interpret the quick (liquid or acid-test) ratio.
Analyse how a transaction changes the current ratio.

topics.title: Solvency ratios

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate and interpret the debt-equity ratio.
Calculate the proprietary, debt to capital employed and total assets to debt ratios.
Calculate and interpret the interest coverage ratio.

topics.title: Activity (turnover) ratios

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate and interpret the inventory turnover ratio.
Calculate trade receivables and payables turnover ratios with collection and payment periods.
Interpret net assets, fixed assets and working capital turnover ratios.

topics.title: Profitability ratios

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate gross profit, operating and net profit ratios.
Calculate and interpret return on investment and return on shareholders' funds.
Calculate earnings per share, book value per share, dividend payout and P/E ratios.

topics.title: Objectives and benefits of the cash flow statement

concepts.learning_objective: State the objective of a cash flow statement prepared under AS-3 and its place among the financial statements.
Explain how a cash flow statement helps users assess liquidity, solvency and comparability.

topics.title: Cash, cash equivalents and cash flows

concepts.learning_objective: Identify items that qualify as cash and cash equivalents as per AS-3.
Distinguish transactions that are cash flows from movements within cash and cash equivalents.

topics.title: Classification into operating, investing and financing activities

concepts.learning_objective: Identify cash flows arising from the principal revenue-generating activities of an enterprise.
Classify cash flows from acquisition and disposal of long-term assets and investments.
Classify cash flows that change the size and composition of owners' capital and borrowings.

topics.title: Treatment of some peculiar items

concepts.learning_objective: Classify interest and dividend paid and received for financial and non-financial enterprises.
Classify income taxes and extraordinary items in a cash flow statement.
Recognise investing and financing transactions that are excluded because they involve no cash.

topics.title: Cash flow from operating activities: indirect method

concepts.learning_objective: Work out net profit before tax and extraordinary items from given balances.
Adjust net profit for non-cash and non-operating items to find operating profit before working capital changes.
Adjust for changes in current assets and current liabilities to arrive at cash generated from operations.

topics.title: Investing and financing cash flows and preparing the statement

concepts.learning_objective: Compute cash flows from investing activities using asset accounts and additional information.
Compute cash flows from financing activities from changes in capital and borrowings.
Prepare the cash flow statement format and reconcile opening and closing cash and cash equivalents.
